case_title.quote: STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR. v. NARAYAN @ NARAYAN SAI @ MOTA BHAGWAN
case_title.reason: Case title matches the judgment header; spacing differs only through OCR.

number_of_accused.quote: The appeal arises from a judgment of a Single Judge... directed the release of the respondent
number_of_accused.reason: Only one respondent is before the Court in this matter.

accused_gender.quote: The respondent is the only son of his father.
accused_gender.reason: Respondent is referred to with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age of the respondent appears anywhere in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: Religion of the respondent is not mentioned.

accused_caste.reason: Caste of the respondent is not mentioned.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation of the respondent is not stated.

accused_socioeconomic_status.correct_value: Judgment refers to a financial background and crores of rupees of properties seized, invested on his behalf
accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: has a network of persons and a financial background
accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: Judgment does reference the respondent's financial background and seized investments, so 'Not stated' is contradicted.

previous_criminal_record.correct_value: Seven offences registered against him, with illegal jail activities, bribery attempts and witness threats attributed to him or followers
previous_criminal_record.quote: seven offences have been registered against him
previous_criminal_record.reason: Omits the seven registered offences; threats and assaults on witnesses were by followers, not the respondent himself.

victim_gender.quote: compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- ... to the prosecutrix
victim_gender.reason: The complainant/prosecutrix is female, so the victim is female.

victim_age.reason: No age of the prosecutrix is given in the judgment.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: The judgment does not describe any relationship between respondent and prosecutrix.

offence_category.quote: Respondent is accused in high profile cases of rape and atrocities
offence_category.reason: Rape under s.376(2)(c) IPC is the principal offence of conviction.

statutory_provisions.reason: Omits s.323 IPC, which is among the convictions listed.

weapon.correct_value: No weapon used in the convicted offences; lethal weapon and revolver used by others against witnesses
weapon.quote: was assaulted with a lethal weapon on 28 February 2014
weapon.reason: Weapons are mentioned, but only in attacks on witnesses by others, not the convicted offences.

evidence_type.reason: The judgment does not discuss the evidence type for the convicted offences.

confession.reason: Judgment is silent on confession; 'None' asserts an absence it never states.

aggravating_circumstances.quote: The respondent and his father have a mass following of persons who owe loyalty to them
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Listed aggravating circumstances match the DGP grounds endorsed in the judgment.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: No untoward incident took place after the respondent was released in December 2020
mitigating_circumstances.reason: High Court noted no untoward incident and the mother's health was the basis for release.

trial_court_outcome.quote: the Sessions Court by a judgment dated 30 April 2019 convicted the respondent
trial_court_outcome.reason: Conviction with life imprisonment and fine is stated.

high_court_outcome.quote: Allowing the application of the respondent, the Single Judge of the High Court held
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court allowed the application and directed furlough.

final_outcome.correct_value: Appeal by State allowed; High Court judgment and order of 24 June 2021 set aside
final_outcome.quote: we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court dated 24 June 2021
final_outcome.reason: Respondent was not acquitted; the Supreme Court allowed the State's appeal against furlough.

offence_finally_established.correct_value: Trial conviction under IPC ss.376(2)(c), 377, 354, 504, 506(2), 508 and 323 stands; appeal against it pending in High Court
offence_finally_established.quote: The appeal against the respondent's conviction and the application for suspension of sentence are pending
offence_finally_established.reason: Conviction was not set aside; the judgment records it as standing with appeal pending.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Life imprisonment and rigorous imprisonment (various terms)
imprisonment_type.quote: (i) Section 376(2): life imprisonment together with a fine
imprisonment_type.reason: Judgment records life and rigorous imprisonment sentences, not 'none'.

imprisonment_years.reason: Sentence is life imprisonment, which has no fixed term in years.

fine_rs.quote: together with a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Fines were imposed under each conviction; value null contradicts the judgment.

neutral_facts.correct_value: The respondent was convicted of rape and other IPC offences in 2019 and was in custody. During trial, attempts were made to bribe officials and threaten witnesses. He was granted furlough in December 2020 and interim bail in early 2021. The DGP denied furlough on public peace grounds; the High Court allowed it.
neutral_facts.quote: The High Court allowed the furlough leave, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision
neutral_facts.reason: Summary reveals the Supreme Court's outcome and invents 'cruelty' as an offence, which the judgment does not state.

offence_severity.quote: (i) Section 376(2): life imprisonment together with a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/-
offence_severity.reason: Seven sentence entries listed match the conviction summary in the judgment.

attempt_completion.reason: Convictions for the listed offences imply completed offences; no attempt-only finding is made.

physical_harm.correct_value: Witnesses injured and one killed by others in attacks linked to followers; no physical harm described for the convicted offences
physical_harm.quote: The witness suffered severe injury and died during treatment.
physical_harm.reason: Harm is accurately described but was caused by unknown persons or followers, not in the convicted offences.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Seven offences registered against him; seven convictions recorded under IPC sections listed
number_of_offences.quote: seven offences have been registered against him
number_of_offences.reason: Judgment records seven convictions, so 'finally upheld' count is stated, not absent.

financial_property_loss.correct_value: Compensation of Rs 5,00,000 to prosecutrix under s.357(3) CrPC; crores of rupees of properties seized, linked to investments on respondent's behalf
financial_property_loss.quote: The respondent was directed to pay compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/-
financial_property_loss.reason: Judgment records compensation and seized properties worth crores, so 'Not applicable' is contradicted.

premeditation_planning.correct_value: Attempts to threaten and suborn investigating team and witnesses noted; Court made no premeditation finding
premeditation_planning.quote: An attempt has been made to threaten and suborn the investigating team and the witnesses.
premeditation_planning.reason: Attempts are accurately noted, but 'premeditation and planning' is not a finding in the judgment.

motive.reason: No motive for the convicted offences is discussed.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Court held the DGP's opinion not perverse and based on relevant circumstances; it did not formally accept evidence
key_evidence_accepted.quote: The opinion of the Sanctioning Authority under the Rules does not suffer from perversity
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Circumstances are accurately listed, but the Court reviewed the DGP's opinion rather than accepting evidence.

witness_credibility.correct_value: No witness credibility assessment made; Court noted DGP's circumstances on threats to witnesses and conduct in jail
witness_credibility.quote: The conduct after the trial, in jail, has not been shown to be above reproach.
witness_credibility.reason: Court recorded the DGP's circumstances but did not assess any witness's credibility.

post_offence_conduct.quote: The respondent was released on temporary bail for a period of three weeks on 16 April 2015
post_offence_conduct.reason: Bail, furlough and surrender dates match the judgment.

custody_duration.quote: The respondent has been under imprisonment for a period of seven and a half years.
custody_duration.reason: High Court noted seven and a half years of imprisonment.

bail_history.correct_value: Temporary bail 16 April 2015 (three weeks) and 15 February 2019 (two days); interim bail 31 January to 3 February 2021
bail_history.quote: released on temporary bail from 31 January 2021 to 3 February 2021
bail_history.reason: Only the 2021 interim bail is listed; 2015 and 2019 temporary bail periods are omitted.

trial_duration.correct_value: FIR 6 October 2013; trial judgment 30 April 2019; High Court furlough order 2 December 2020; impugned High Court order 24 June 2021
trial_duration.quote: registered against the respondent on 6 October 2013
trial_duration.reason: FIR date mislabelled as offence date; 2 December 2020 was a furlough order, not a judgment.

legal_representation.quote: Tushar Mehta, SG, Kanu Agrawal, Aniruddha P. Mayee, Advs. for the Appellants.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names for both sides match the judgment.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered; charges framed; trial concluded
investigation_status.quote: Charges were framed. On the conclusion of the trial
investigation_status.reason: Charge sheet filing is not stated; charges framed and trial conclusion are.

procedural_irregularity.reason: No procedural irregularity is identified by the Court.

appeal_history.quote: The Single Judge directed the release of the respondent on furlough.
appeal_history.reason: Trial conviction, High Court furlough order, and Supreme Court allowance are accurately summarised.

prosecution_argument.quote: Furlough can be denied if it is not in the interest of the society
prosecution_argument.reason: State's argument on public peace, criminal history and witness threats is accurately summarised.

defence_argument.correct_value: Furlough is a matter of right; no untoward incident since release; prior offences unconnected to respondent; prior furlough order valid
defence_argument.quote: The furlough leave is a matter of right
defence_argument.reason: Omits the matter-of-right argument and the claim that respondent is not connected to other offences.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the grant of furlough must be balanced against the public interest and can be refused to certain categories of prisoners.
legal_principle_applied.reason: Discretionary nature and public interest balancing reflect the Court's stated principles.

precedent_relied_upon.reason: The three cases and citations match the judgment.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Judgment gives no sentencing rationale; 'Not applicable' is consistent.

judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: Court identifies no mitigating factor in sentencing terms; 'None' is consistent.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Cumulative circumstances indicating risk to public peace: threats to witnesses, mass following, attempts to bribe officials, conduct in jail
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: The order dated 8 May 2021 has adduced a number of circumstances which cumulatively indicate
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court expressly relied on aggravating circumstances in upholding the DGP's opinion, so 'None' is contradicted.

other_sentence_order.reason: No further sentence order is made; the Court only sets aside the High Court order.
